attribution.note: The sentence is in Marcus's own Substack essay, co-written with Davis, and stated in the authors' own voice. It is not quoting anyone else.

semantics.note: The drafter keeps the scope ('all or most', 'recent' demos) and the word 'apparently'. Here 'apparently' signals reliance on reports, not a probability, so this stays a scorable observation about past demos.

contract.note: Tying it to We Robot (Oct 10, 2024) and separating interactive judgment from locomotion is a fair, ordinary reading of 'commonsense'. The demos are not named and 'all or most' has no measure, so interpretation matters.

evidence.note: Ars Technica, Oct 15, 2024, citing Bloomberg and an engineer via Scoble. It reports that chatting, pouring drinks and games were remotely assisted, while walking ran on AI. This matches the support condition.

Kovac's post is a Tesla disclosure. It admits the robots were human-assisted 'to some extent' and says walking, balance and dancing were autonomous. That concerns motor control, not interactive judgment, so it does not contradict the claim. It does not say which tasks were assisted.

reviews.rationale: Independent reporting (e1) says humans remotely ran the interactive tasks at We Robot: conversation, drink service and games. The only autonomous functions it identifies are walking and balance, which Tesla's own statement (e2) confirms. That meets the support condition. One caveat: the evidence covers We Robot only, not every late-2024 Optimus demo.
